coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: You're 37 days out and in taper—this is not a day to prove fitness. Easy 6–7 miles on rolling terrain at Z2 (130–140 bpm, conversational effort). Your last three runs average 138–140 bpm; today should feel noticeably slower and shorter. Wednesday's traditional hill slot is scaled back in taper; use gentle rollers to maintain neuromuscular sharpness without accumulated fatigue. Keep it under 60 min total. You've got 19.1 miles in the bank already this week; a modest Wednesday run sets you up for a proper long effort this weekend.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Your recovery score is solid (76/100) and your RHR is down to 62 bpm—clean signs your body is adapting well. Fuel conservatively today: 200–250g carbs spread across meals, emphasis on post-run glycogen (40–50g carbs + 20g protein within 30 min of finishing). Your sleep efficiency dropped to 62.4% last night despite 7.5 hours; likely stress or travel. Dial sodium intake up slightly to aid sleep osmolality—aim for 2,000–2,500 mg today—and front-load carbs at breakfast and lunch to stabilize afternoon energy for evening calls.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep quality matters more than duration right now. You averaged 8.2 hours over 30 days but hit only 62% efficiency last night—that's fragmentation, not restorative sleep. Tonight: no screens after 9 p.m., room temp 65–67°F, blackout. You're in taper; your body wants recovery more than volume. Your HRV has no recent data, so we can't read nervous-system strain directly, but your RHR trend (62 vs. 65-day avg) suggests parasympathetic tone is building. Protect that with 8+ hours of quality sleep and zero sleep debt heading into race week.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Taper anxiety is real for driven athletes. You're dropping volume hard (19 miles in 5 days vs. 47 last week), and your executive brain will scream that you're losing fitness. You're not. The Julian Alps 50K demands 2,500m of vert on technical terrain—that's endurance-dependent, not speed-dependent. Your aerobic base is locked in. Use these next 37 days to finalize alpine-specific nutrition (How many gels between aid stations? What's your calorie rate on steep climbs?), confirm your gear in actual vertical (test your quads, feet, pack), and sleep. Trust the plan, not the taper voice.
